analysis.title: AI Agent Engineer, Workforce Experience
analysis.fit_rationale: The candidate has strong professional evidence in Python, ETL, data pipelines, and reporting automation, plus project-level experience with agentic workflows, RAG, and LLM tooling (Claude Code, MCP). The role's core (60%) requires production multi-agent workflow design, stakeholder translation, reliability, cost ownership, and documentation—areas where the candidate has transferable skills but limited direct production AI agent experience. The workforce experience focus (40%) aligns with the candidate's current work on internal tooling, AI-assisted reporting, and knowledge base research, though adoption/enablement and intake/self-service are not explicitly evidenced. The candidate's background in capacity/performance engineering and data engineering provides a strong foundation for the technical aspects, but the lack of demonstrated production multi-agent workflow deployment and internal tooling adoption metrics lowers the score.
strengths: Expert-level Python and SQL with extensive ETL and data pipeline experience (CITI, Sabre).
Proven ability to translate requirements into workflows and reports for non-technical stakeholders (capacity reporting, forecasting).
Hands-on project experience with agentic workflows, RAG, FAISS, MCP, and Claude Code (AI job-search pipeline, lakehouse Text-to-SQL agent).
Current role involves AI-assisted automation of reporting and data integration (JIRA, SQL Server, Splunk, Power BI).
Strong troubleshooting and monitoring skills from performance engineering (Dynatrace, CA APM).
Experience building internal tooling and knowledge base concepts (LLM-enabled team knowledge base research).
gaps: No explicit evidence of building and deploying a production multi-agent workflow with handoff and context sharing.
Limited evidence of driving adoption, enablement, or training for AI capabilities (no office hours, power-user community, or measured adoption).
No demonstrated experience with intake or self-service mechanisms that reduce manual request handling.
No explicit experience with cost optimization of AI workloads (prompt tightening, caching, deterministic steps).
No evidence of defining accuracy standards, human review checkpoints, or escalation criteria for AI outputs.
No direct experience in government/defense or intelligence workflows (OSINT, DIGINT, zero-trust).
tailoring_plan: 1. Rewrite headline to emphasize 'AI Agent Engineer with production data pipeline and agentic workflow project experience.' 2. In the summary, highlight the AI job-search pipeline and lakehouse Text-to-SQL agent as evidence of multi-agent design, RAG, and tool calling. 3. Under current role, emphasize the AI-assisted reporting automation as internal tooling that improves efficiency, and mention the LLM knowledge base research as a step toward self-service. 4. Add a 'Relevant Projects' section detailing the agentic pipeline: architecture, agent handoff, context sharing, failure modes, and fixes
